text:
sophia: seeing a big throughput drop across several dedicated pools, started ~12:05 UTC. multiple worker restarts and GPU OOMs. nvml shows memory jumping then process dies. anyone else? :eyes:
rajeev: saw the alert. which model + runtime variant? any recent kernel-selector or batching changes?
emily: model is rwd-13b-qa, runtime variant v3-quant. we rolled kernel-selector v3 last night (auto-rollout). batching heuristic was also tweaked to prefer lower-latency single-batch windows.
sophia: logs attached: 
```
[2026-03-17T12:05:10Z] worker=svc-75 pid=12345 ERR OOM: cudaMalloc failed, tried 536870912 bytes
[2026-03-17T12:05:10Z] worker=svc-75 INFO restarting worker (oom)
[2026-03-17T12:05:11Z] gpu-mon nvml: pid=12345 mem=31457280000 bytes
```
rajeev: interesting — profiler snapshot shows allocator fragmentation spikes after kernel switch. nvprof samples: "alloc_rounds": +42%, "largest_free_block": down to 32Mi on some GPUs.
emily: KV cache hit-rate dropped from ~92% to ~14% at the same time — more KV population churn => more allocations. maybe batching tweak created many small prefix-only batches causing lots of tiny allocations and slab splitting.
sophia: so chain of events hypothesis: batching heuristic -> more tiny batches -> allocator slab fragmentation -> kernel selector picks fallback kernels -> higher mem usage -> OOM + restarts -> throughput drop.
rajeev: that matches the flamegraph I grabbed. kernel v3 uses an aggressive fused-kernel path that keeps some temporary buffers pinned per-stream; when allocator can't coalesce, those pins accumulate.
ops-bot: INCIDENT ALERT: high-error-rate in pool dedicated-west-2 (https://internal.redwood/incident/INC-4521)
sophia: can we revert kernel-selector to v2 for affected pools? rollback safe?
emily: yes, v2 is still in the catalog. I'll push a canary revert to one zone. also increasing batch consolidation window to 30ms to reduce small-batch density.
rajeev: also suggest enabling slab-coalescing GC (experimental) for these workers — trades a bit of latency for lower fragmentation. I'll open a runtime PR and tag infra.
sophia: running a short profile after canary revert. attaching quick pmap: 
```
GPU0 free lists: 18 slabs, avg_frag=0.62, largest_free=48Mi
GPU0 after revert: 26 slabs, avg_frag=0.14, largest_free=220Mi
```
emily: after revert canary: no OOMs in the last 7m for canary hosts, throughput recovered ~82% of baseline. KV hit-rate back to 88%.
sophia: great. let's keep canary for 30m then roll. add a follow-up to tune batching heuristics to avoid tiny-batch hotpaths and add a perf regression test for kernel-selector changes.
rajeev: noted. PR and rollback docs in the incident ticket. I'll add a quick reproduction harness to simulate small-batch density.
sophia: thanks. filing postmortem with root cause = allocator fragmentation exacerbated by batching heuristic and new kernel variant; mitigations: revert kernel-selector, increase consolidation window, enable slab coalesce GC, perf-test for small-batch workloads. :thumbsup:
